correctness.rationale: The abelian ideal D=⟨z,w⟩ and ad_x(z)=w give the exhaustive lift classification. For an x-slope the intersection with D must be 0, ⟨w⟩ or D; a pure y-projection permits any intersection; independent projections force z modulo w and then w, giving the whole algebra. Counting the lifts gives q³+3q²+3q+5. Cross-brackets are the xy and xz coordinate minors, valid also in characteristic two. For two X₀ lines, unequal slopes give no vertical intersection and a nonzero z-component; equal slopes fail exactly for distinct z-coefficients, when the needed w is outside their vertical line. For X₀/X₁ and X₁/X₁ only unequal slopes fail, as their vertical part is then ⟨w⟩. For X versus Y the projections are independent: X₀ fails with Y₀ or either Y₁ family, and X₁ fails with Y₀ or Y₁ containing w, but the other Y₁ family supplies a second independent vertical direction. X₀ against a noncentral line in D is the remaining failure. The other pairs commute or have enough of D to contain every cross-bracket. Counting both orientations where needed gives q³(q³+6q²+4q+1), and subtraction from the square of the lattice size and expansion give the stated probability and asymptotic. The frozen RREF verifier and its recorded fields q=2,3,4,5,7 were inspected, not executed. Its finite coverage, including the genuine field GF(4), is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The all-field subalgebra statistic is well motivated, and the contrast with class-two examples is meaningful in isolation. As a separate narrow exact finding, though, the lattice size and probability do not fill an exact-fact gap in the compared record set: the available dimension-refined enumeration already yields the entire claimed invariant and its asymptotic. A different pair-count proof does not by itself supply another useful invariant as the frozen finding.
